answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require every identity to post collateral that is slashed when duplicate accounts are detected. An attacker minting a thousand fake agents must lock a thousand deposits, so the cost of flooding grows linearly with each fabricated account. Even a long voyage of cheap registrations ends in a cold oasis of no profit, because honest stakers recover their collateral while attackers forfeit reserves hard as onyx. Duplicate identities surface when their shared stake source is traced on-chain.
